aiItems.content:
What is 3 piece wall art?

3 piece wall art is a coordinated set of three individual art prints designed to be displayed together as a group, creating a unified visual statement on your wall. Each print in the set shares a common colour palette, theme, or style so they look intentional and cohesive side by side. You can hang them in a straight horizontal row, a staggered arrangement, or even spread across a larger wall for a gallery effect. They're a brilliant choice when you want to fill a wide space — like above a fireplace or along a hallway — without the guesswork of mixing different prints yourself. Because the hard work of matching is already done, a set of 3 is one of the easiest ways to create a polished, decorator-level look in any room.

How to Hang 3 Piece Wall Art Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall space first: Use a tape measure to find the width of your chimney breast or the wall space above the fireplace. Aim for your three prints together to span roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of that width — wide enough to feel balanced, but with breathing room on either side.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of the wall lightly with a pencil. Your middle print should be centred on this point. This keeps the whole arrangement visually anchored and symmetrical above the mantel.

3. Set your hanging height: The bottom edge of your prints should sit roughly 15–20 cm above the mantel shelf. This keeps them connected to the fireplace as a feature rather than floating too high up the wall.

4. Space the prints evenly: Leave a consistent gap between each print — 4–6 cm is a good rule of thumb for a neat, intentional look. Use a spirit level to make sure all three are perfectly aligned horizontally before you commit to the fixings.

5. Step back and check: Before making any permanent marks, hold the prints up against the wall (or use paper templates cut to size) and step back to see how the arrangement looks at a distance. Adjust the height or spacing if anything feels off — it's much easier now than after the nails are in.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Your Choices

Unframed Print — The print only, shipped flat and ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want to match a very specific frame style or colour. Available in Luster or Museum quality art paper.

Framed Print — Arrives fully assembled and ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping, no measuring, no fuss. The most convenient option if you want the set on the wall as quickly as possible. Available in Luster or Museum quality art paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed on canvas and stretched around a wooden frame — no glass, no mount, just the art itself with a tactile, painted feel. Arrives ready to hang and suits the oil-painting aesthetic of this bohemian book set particularly well. Available in multiple sizes.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish with a gentle sheen that makes warm earthy tones and greens pop. Works beautifully in naturally lit rooms such as a study or sitting room above the fireplace.

Museum Quality Paper — A smooth, flat matte finish with a gallery feel. Ideal for rooms with more atmospheric, lower lighting, or for anyone who wants the art to look as close to an original painting as possible.

What is canvas 3 piece wall art?

Canvas 3 piece wall art is a set of three coordinating art prints designed to be displayed together as a group, creating a cohesive and visually balanced arrangement on your wall. Each print in the set shares a common theme, colour palette or style so that, hung side by side, they look like one considered, intentional display rather than three random pieces. The term 'canvas' is used broadly — the set can come as wrapped canvas prints, framed prints or unframed prints on art paper, depending on the finish you prefer. They are particularly popular for hallways, living rooms, study rooms and reading nooks because a set of three fills a wall with personality in a way a single print simply cannot. Choosing a set also takes the guesswork out of curating a gallery wall yourself — the hard work of matching colours and subjects is already done for you.

How to Hang Canvas 3 Piece Wall Art in a Hallway or Reading Nook

1. Measure your wall first: Note the full width of the wall you want to use. Aim for the combined width of all three prints plus the gaps between them to fill roughly two-thirds of that space — this gives the set visual weight without overwhelming the room.

2. Mark your centre point: Find the centre of the wall and use a pencil mark or a strip of painter's tape to mark it. Your middle print should sit centred on this point, making the whole arrangement balanced and symmetrical.

3. Decide on your gaps: A gap of 5–8 cm between each print is the sweet spot for a neat, gallery-style look. Use strips of card cut to that width as spacers while you mark your hanging points — it keeps everything even without lots of measuring.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of the middle print should sit at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is the standard eye-level guideline that works for most people and most rooms. In a hallway with lower ceilings, you can drop this slightly.

5. Check alignment with a spirit level: Before you commit to the final nails or fixings, hold each print up in position and use a small spirit level or a level app on your phone to make sure all three are perfectly straight and level with each other. This is the step most people skip — and it really does make a difference to the finished look.

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A versatile, cost-effective option that lets you choose your own frame. Luster paper gives a subtle sheen that makes colours pop and handles light well — great for everyday display in hallways or study rooms.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The premium paper choice for collectors and those who want the sharpest, most gallery-accurate colour reproduction. A heavier, fine-art finish that looks stunning when framed and is built to last for years.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum Quality) — Arrives ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping needed. The frame and print are matched and fitted for you, which is ideal if you want a clean, polished result without the hassle of sourcing a frame separately. Available in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a textured, painterly feel that suits the oil-painting style of this bohemian books set particularly well. No frame needed — the canvas wraps around the edges and hangs as-is. A great choice if you want something that feels more like original artwork on your wall.

aiItems.content:
What is artwork for the living room?

Artwork for the living room refers to any wall art print, canvas or framed image chosen specifically to suit a living space — enhancing its personality, colour scheme and atmosphere. The best living room art reflects the people who live there, whether that's bold abstract colour, calming botanicals or, as with this bohemian books set, a warm and personal still-life scene that celebrates everyday pleasures like reading and a good cup of tea. Living room wall art typically comes as single prints, pairs or sets — a set of three, like this one, is particularly popular because it fills a wall with a cohesive story without requiring you to mix and match different pieces yourself. Choosing art for the living room is really about finding something that feels right for the space and genuinely right for you.

How to Hang and Style Artwork for the Living Room: A Simple Step-by-Step

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall that gets good natural or artificial light and where the prints will be at eye level when you're seated — above a sofa, beside a reading chair or over a console table are all great spots for this set.

2. Measure your space: Hold the three prints up against the wall (or use paper cut-outs the same size) to check they'll fill roughly two-thirds of the wall width. Mark the centre point of your display with a light pencil dot.

3. Map out the layout: Lay the three prints on the floor in front of the wall to plan your spacing. A gap of 5–8 cm between each print looks balanced — close enough to read as a set, with enough breathing room to appreciate each one individually.

4. Hang the centre print first: Fix the middle print at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print is the standard guide). Use a spirit level to make sure it's straight.

5. Add the outer prints: Working outwards from the centre, hang the left and right prints at exactly the same height, maintaining your chosen gap. Step back and check the alignment — adjust as needed before any marks become permanent.

6. Style around them: These prints work beautifully with warm-toned accessories — think natural wood, wicker baskets, a cosy throw or a small stack of real books on a shelf below. Let the art lead the room's colour story.

Which Option Is Right for You? Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas

Finish — Unframed print: print only, you choose and source your own frame. Framed print: arrives complete and ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: artwork printed and stretched over a wooden frame, no additional framing needed.

Effort to hang — Unframed print: requires your own frame and fitting. Framed print: ready to hang straight out of the box. Wrapped canvas: ready to hang straight out of the box.

Paper / material choice — Unframed print: available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Framed print: available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: canvas material — no paper option.

Look and feel — Unframed print: flexible — suits any frame style you choose. Framed print: clean, polished, gallery-ready finish. Wrapped canvas: painterly, textured, gallery-wrap appearance with no frame required.

Best for — Unframed print: those who already have frames or want full control over the framing style. Framed print: anyone who wants a fuss-free, complete result. Wrapped canvas: those who love a natural, painted-art aesthetic on the wall.

aiItems.content:
What is 3 piece wall art framed?

A 3 piece wall art framed set is a group of three coordinating art prints designed to be displayed together as a single arrangement on your wall. Each print shares a common colour palette, theme or style so that the trio looks cohesive and considered rather than random. You can hang them in a horizontal row, a vertical column, or even in a stepped arrangement depending on your wall space. Framed sets are especially popular above a fireplace, sofa or bed because they fill a wide wall beautifully while keeping things visually balanced and unified.

How to Hang 3 Piece Wall Art Framed Above a Fireplace

1. Measure your wall: Start by measuring the width of your chimney breast or the wall space above your fireplace. As a guide, aim for the full spread of all three prints to cover roughly two thirds of that width — this keeps things balanced and stops the set looking too small or too crowded.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of the wall and mark it lightly with a pencil. The middle print should sit centred on this point, with the two flanking prints placed at an even distance on either side — a gap of around 5 to 8 cm between each print looks neat and intentional.

3. Set your hanging height: The centre of the middle print should sit roughly at eye level, or around 15 to 20 cm above the mantelpiece shelf — whichever feels more balanced in your room. Hold the prints up against the wall before committing to make sure you're happy with the height.

4. Use a spirit level: Before you hammer any nails, use a spirit level or a free smartphone app to make sure all three prints are perfectly aligned horizontally. Even a small tilt can make the whole arrangement look off, so it's worth taking an extra minute here.

5. Step back and adjust: Once hung, step back and look at the set from across the room — this is the view most people will have. Small tweaks to spacing or height at this stage make a big difference to the finished look.

Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas — Which Option is Right for You?

Ready to hang straight away — Framed print: Yes, arrives ready to hang. Wrapped canvas: Yes, arrives ready to hang. Unframed print: No — you source and fit your own frame or mount.

Frame included — Framed print: Yes. Wrapped canvas: No frame; the print wraps around a deep wooden stretcher bar. Unframed print: No.

Best for a gallery or painted look — Framed print: Gallery look with a defined border. Wrapped canvas: Painterly, frameless feel — great for a bohemian or relaxed style. Unframed print: Flexible — style it however you like.

Paper / surface choice — Framed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Unframed print: Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Wrapped canvas: Canvas wrap (no paper option).

Ideal if you — Framed print: Want a neat, finished look with no extra effort. Wrapped canvas: Love a more relaxed, contemporary feel. Unframed print: Already have a favourite frame or prefer to customise the presentation yourself.

aiItems.content:
What is framed 3 piece wall art?

Framed 3 piece wall art is a coordinated set of three individual art prints designed to be displayed together as one cohesive arrangement on your wall. Each print in the set shares the same colour palette, style or theme so that when hung side by side — or in another arrangement that suits your space — they look intentional and complete. Unlike buying individual prints separately, a set of 3 gives you an instant, ready-to-style grouping with no guesswork about whether pieces will complement each other. At AboutWallArt, our sets are available as unframed prints, framed prints or wrapped canvases in a range of sizes, so you can tailor the look entirely to your home.

How to Hang Framed 3 Piece Wall Art in a Hallway or Study

1. Measure your wall first: Use a tape measure to find the width of your wall space. Aim for the combined width of all three prints (plus the gaps between them) to fill around two thirds of the available width — this gives a balanced, considered look rather than feeling either too cramped or too sparse.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall space and mark it lightly with a pencil. Hang the middle print first, centred on that mark at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print). This gives you a fixed anchor to work outward from.

3. Space the outer prints evenly: Measure an even gap of 5–8 cm from the edge of the centre print and position the left and right prints at exactly the same height. Use a spirit level to keep all three aligned horizontally — even a small tilt is noticeable once the prints are up.

4. Step back and adjust: Before you commit to the final fixings, hold or lightly tack each print in place and step back to check the overall look. In a hallway, natural light changes through the day, so check at different times if you can — the moody grey tones in this set can shift beautifully depending on the light.

Choosing Your Format: Unframed Print, Framed Print or Wrapped Canvas

Unframed Print — The print only, on your choice of Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Great if you already have frames you love or want to choose your own framing to match your existing décor. You'll need to source and fit your own frames.

Framed Print — Your chosen print on Luster or Museum quality paper, supplied ready to hang — no extra trips to find a frame that fits. A brilliant time-saver and the most popular choice for hallways where you want a polished, finished look straight away.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, arriving ready to hang. No paper, no glass — just a clean, contemporary look with real texture and depth. Ideal if you prefer a more relaxed, bohemian feel without the formality of a framed print.

Paper finish (prints only) — Luster art paper has a gentle semi-sheen that makes colours look vivid and rich. Museum quality paper is a premium matt finish with exceptional colour accuracy and fine detail — perfect for viewing up close in a reading nook or study.

aiItems.content:
What is a canvas painting for living room?

A canvas painting for living room is a decorative art print or wrapped canvas designed to add colour, personality and warmth to your main living space. They come in a wide range of styles — from abstract and botanical to still-life and bohemian — and are available as single pieces or coordinating sets. Sets of three are particularly popular because they create an instant gallery-wall effect without the guesswork of mixing and matching individual pieces. Whether printed on art paper with a frame or stretched over a canvas wrap, they are one of the quickest and most effective ways to pull a room together and make it feel truly like home.

How to Hang a Canvas Painting for Living Room: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold a piece of tape or use painter's tape on the wall to mark out the rough footprint of all three prints together, including the gaps between them. Step back and check you are happy with the placement before making any holes.

2. Find the right height: The centre of your set should sit roughly at eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor is the standard guide for most living rooms. If hanging above a sofa or console, leave about 20–25 cm of space between the top of the furniture and the bottom of the prints.

3. Space the prints evenly: For a clean, gallery look, keep the gap between each of the three prints consistent — 5 to 8 cm is usually ideal. Use a spirit level or a free levelling app on your phone to keep everything straight.

4. Mark and hang: Lightly mark each hanging point in pencil, fix your hooks or picture nails, and hang the prints one at a time, checking the level as you go. Framed and canvas-wrapped options come ready to hang, so no extra hardware is needed.

5. Stand back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back across the room and check the spacing and level with fresh eyes. Small adjustments make a big difference to the finished look.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Our Canvas Painting for Living Room Formats

Unframed Print on Luster Art Paper — A versatile option if you already have frames at home or prefer to choose your own. Luster paper gives a soft sheen that enhances the depth of dark, moody artwork like this set. Post flat in protective packaging.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — A matte, fine-art finish that reduces glare — ideal if your living room receives strong natural or artificial light. Crisp, gallery-standard results with no shine.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum Quality) — Arrives completely ready to hang straight out of the packaging — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A great all-in-one solution if you want a polished, finished look immediately.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a solid frame, giving a relaxed, studio-art feel. No frame or glass required — just hang and enjoy. Available in its own range of sizes and suits bohemian or casual-eclectic interiors especially well.

What is bar wall art decor?

Bar wall art decor refers to printed artwork designed to bring personality and style to a home bar area, bar cart, or any living space with a drinks or entertaining theme. How to Hang Bar Wall Art Decor: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Pick the wall you want to use — above a sofa, a bar cart or a sideboard works brilliantly. Measure the width of the space and divide by three to work out roughly how wide each print should be, leaving equal gaps between them.

2. Select your size and finish: Decide whether you want a smaller, more delicate arrangement or a larger, bolder statement. Luster paper suits rooms with natural light; Museum quality paper suits brighter or more formal spaces; wrapped canvas suits a contemporary, frameless look.

3. Mark your hanging points: Hold the first print up to the wall at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of the print is a good guide). Mark lightly with a pencil. Repeat for the other two, keeping the gaps even — around 5–8 cm between each print is ideal.

4. Hang and level: Use appropriate wall fixings for your wall type. Once all three are up, use a spirit level to check they are aligned, and step back to make sure the spacing looks even from a distance.

5. Style around them: Add a drinks tray, some glassware or a small plant on a shelf or bar cart below the prints to tie the whole look together and really make the bar wall art decor sing.

Format — Unframed Print: You receive the art print only, ready for you to frame in a frame of your own choosing. Perfect if you already have frames or want to match existing decor precisely.

Format — Framed Print: The print arrives ready to hang straight out of the packaging — no need to source a separate frame. A great time-saver and the most popular choice for gifting.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary, frameless look. Ideal for modern or minimalist interiors.

Paper — Luster Art Paper: A semi-gloss finish that makes colours appear vibrant and rich. Works beautifully in rooms with natural light where you want the pastel tones to really glow.

Paper — Museum Quality Paper: A premium matt finish with a refined, gallery-like feel. A great choice if your room gets strong direct light or if you prefer a more understated, sophisticated look.

aiItems.content:
What is modern living room wall art?

Modern living room wall art refers to prints, canvases or framed artwork designed specifically to complement contemporary home interiors — typically featuring clean lines, a considered colour palette and a style that feels current rather than traditional. It can range from abstract and geometric pieces to travel-inspired cityscapes, botanical illustrations or minimalist photography, all chosen to add personality and visual interest to a living space. A set of three matching prints — like this Paris cityscape — is one of the most popular formats because it creates a cohesive, gallery-style display without needing any design expertise. The best modern living room wall art works with your existing colours and furniture rather than competing with them, making the whole room feel more pulled-together and intentional.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Paris Wall Art Prints in Your Living Room

1. Measure your wall space: Before anything else, measure the width of the wall or furniture you're hanging above. Aim for the three prints together to cover roughly two-thirds of that width — this gives a balanced, intentional look rather than prints that feel lost on a large wall.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of your wall or sofa with a light pencil dot. The middle print should sit centred on this point, with the left and right prints spaced evenly on either side — a gap of around 5 to 8 cm between each print works well for a cohesive panoramic feel.

3. Set the hanging height: Aim to hang the prints so the vertical centre of each one sits at roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is standard eye level and works whether viewers are standing or sitting on a sofa nearby.

4. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable across three prints in a row. Use a spirit level or a free spirit-level app on your phone to make sure all three are perfectly aligned before you commit to the fixings.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are up, step back to the opposite side of the room and check the overall composition. Small adjustments at this stage are much easier than you think, and getting the spacing just right makes a huge difference to the finished result.

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love, want to match existing decor precisely, or prefer to choose your own mount colour. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives fully assembled and ready to hang straight out of the box — no sourcing frames, no sizing headaches. A brilliant time-saver and the most popular choice for gifting. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched around a wooden frame, giving a gallery-style, frameless look with real texture and depth. Ready to hang immediately. Ideal if you want a more tactile, painterly feel that suits this watercolour cityscape style particularly well.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss finish that handles natural light well and keeps colours vibrant. A great all-round choice for most living rooms.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium matte fine-art paper that brings out exceptional depth and richness in darker tones — particularly well-suited to the deep charcoals and cool greys in this Paris cityscape set.

These pieces tend to use strong contrasts, monochrome palettes or deep rich tones, and they feel at home in hallways, home offices, studies and living rooms where a considered, heritage-inspired look is the goal. What is vintage wall art decor?

Vintage wall art decor refers to art prints that draw on historical imagery, antique objects, aged typography, and classical subjects to bring a sense of heritage and timeless character to a room. It covers everything from old maps and compasses to antique scientific instruments, botanical illustrations, and sepia-toned photography. The appeal is that it feels collected and personal rather than mass-produced — like pieces with a story behind them. In a home office or study, vintage wall art decor is particularly popular because it pairs naturally with dark wood furniture, leather, and classic shelving to create a space that feels both accomplished and genuinely comfortable.

How to Hang Vintage Wall Art Decor as a Diptych in Your Office

1. Choose your wall and measure up: Pick a wall where both prints can sit side by side at eye level — ideally above a desk or a console table. Measure the total width you have available and divide it roughly in thirds: one third for the left print, one third for the gap, one third for the right print. A gap of 5 to 8 cm between the two prints looks intentional without feeling disconnected.

2. Mark your hanging points carefully: Hold one print up against the wall at your chosen height and lightly mark the top edge with a pencil. Use a spirit level across both marks before you put any nails in — even a slight tilt is very noticeable with a diptych. If you're using picture hooks, make sure both hooks are at exactly the same height.

3. Hang and step back: Hang the left print first, then use it as your reference point to position the right one. Step back to the opposite side of the room and check the alignment from a distance — small adjustments are much easier to spot from afar. Once you're happy, tack the prints gently at the back corners with removable adhesive strips to stop them tilting over time.

Paper quality: Museum — A premium fine-art paper with deeper blacks and exceptional sharpness — particularly well suited to these high-detail black and white prints, where every engraved line and cartographic mark counts.

aiItems.content:
What is bathroom wall decor?

Bathroom wall decor refers to any artwork, print, or decorative piece designed to be displayed on the walls of a bathroom, cloakroom, toilet, or spa-style wet room. It's one of the easiest ways to add personality and style to a space that often gets overlooked when it comes to home decorating. The best bathroom wall decor tends to feature calming, nature-inspired or botanical themes — like tropical leaves, florals, or watercolour plants — because these complement the relaxing feel most people want in a bathroom. Choosing the right finish matters too: in a steamy or high-moisture bathroom, canvas-wrapped or well-glazed framed prints hold up far better than unprotected paper prints over time.

How to Hang Bathroom Wall Decor: a Simple Step-by-Step

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough clear space for all three prints — above the bath, along the main wall, or above the sink unit are all great spots. Avoid hanging directly above a shower head where steam hits the wall constantly.

2. Decide on your layout: For a set of three, a horizontal row at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of each print) is the most popular and balanced arrangement. A vertical stack works well in narrow spaces like above the toilet.

3. Mark your positions: Use a pencil and a spirit level to lightly mark where each print will sit. Keep the gaps between prints consistent — around 5–8 cm looks clean and deliberate.

4. Choose the right fixing: For tiled walls, use picture-hanging strips rated for the weight of your prints to avoid drilling. For plastered walls, small picture hooks or nails work well. If you've chosen the canvas-wrapped option, a single D-ring hook per canvas is all you need.

5. Step back and check: Once all three are up, step back and check the alignment from across the room. Adjust any that look slightly off — small tweaks make a big difference to the finished look.

Choosing Your Print Option: Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas?

Unframed Art Print — The print is delivered on its own, ready for you to frame however you like. Great if you have a specific frame style in mind or want to keep costs flexible. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Art Print — Your print arrives ready to hang — no extra framing needed. A brilliant choice for a well-ventilated bathroom where you want a polished, gallery-style finish straight away. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, with multiple size options.

Wrapped Canvas — The print is stretched over a wooden frame, giving a contemporary, frameless look. This is our recommended option for bathrooms and other high-moisture rooms because canvas is moisture-resistant and handles steam and humidity far better than paper prints. Ready to hang on arrival, no frame required. Available in multiple size options.

Paper quality — Luster vs Museum: Luster art paper gives a slight sheen that makes colours pop — great for bold botanical artwork like this set. Museum quality paper has a fine-art matte finish with exceptional colour depth, ideal if you want a premium gallery look. Neither option is metallic or foil — any warm or vivid tones in the artwork are printed ink colours only.

What are botanical prints?

Botanical prints are art prints that depict plants, flowers, leaves, grasses or other natural foliage — typically in a detailed, illustrative or watercolour style inspired by traditional botanical illustration. They have roots in scientific plant documentation from the 17th and 18th centuries, but today they're loved purely for their beauty and the calm, nature-connected feeling they bring to a space. Modern botanical prints range from realistic and delicate to bold and graphic, covering everything from tropical leaves and dried florals to wildflowers and eucalyptus sprigs. They're one of the most versatile styles of wall art available, suiting farmhouse, boho, Scandi, contemporary and classic interiors equally well.

4. Consider your wall colour: The neutral palette of these prints — white, beige and sage green — works with almost any wall colour. White, warm grey, sage and natural linen tones all complement the earthy botanical tones beautifully.

5. Style around them: Once they're up, bring in a small potted plant, a wooden desk accessory or a woven basket nearby — the natural materials echo the botanical theme and tie the whole look together.

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have a frame you love or want to choose your own mount colour. Framed Print — Your chosen print comes ready mounted and framed, arriving ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping required. Choose your paper quality (Luster or Museum) and your preferred size. The most convenient option if you want a polished, finished result with no effort.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame — no glazing, no extra frame needed. This gives a contemporary, gallery-style look and arrives completely ready to hang. A brilliant choice for larger walls or anyone who prefers a frameless, modern finish.

aiItems.content:
What is office art?

Office art refers to wall art prints and decorative pieces chosen specifically to enhance a workspace — whether that's a home office, a professional studio, or a corporate setting. The best office art strikes a balance between personal expression and a tone that supports focus, calm, and creativity. Zen and mindfulness-inspired prints — like Buddha photography and karma quotes — are especially popular because they create a peaceful atmosphere that helps reduce stress during the working day. Unlike purely decorative art, great office art tends to carry a mood or a message that makes the space feel intentional and grounding. A well-chosen set of prints can make even a modest desk area feel considered, inspiring, and genuinely your own.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Office Art Prints for Maximum Impact

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold sheets of paper up to the wall — or use painter's tape — to mark out the rough footprint of three portrait prints side by side. Aim for a consistent gap of 5–10 cm between each print so the set reads as a cohesive group rather than three separate pieces.

2. Find the right height: The centre of the middle print should sit roughly at eye level when you're seated at your desk — usually around 120–130 cm from the floor. This keeps the art in your natural line of sight rather than looming above you or disappearing below your eyeline.

3. Mark and hang in order: Start with the centre print, get it level, then work outward to the left and right. Use a spirit level (even a phone app works well) to keep all three at exactly the same height. Even a centimetre's difference will catch the eye.

4. Step back and assess: Once all three are up, step back to the opposite side of the room and check the spacing and height feel balanced. Adjustments at this stage are easy — and worth taking the time over.

Choosing Your Office Art Print Option: What's the Difference?

Unframed Print — The art print on its own, ready for you to frame however you like. Great if you already have a frame in mind or want to match existing décor exactly. Available in Luster art paper (gentle sheen, warm and rich) or Museum quality paper (flat matte, gallery-like finish).

Framed Print — Your art print arrives ready to hang straight away — no extra shopping required. The framed option saves you the time and effort of sourcing a frame that fits. Available in multiple sizes in Luster or Museum quality paper.

Wrapped Canvas — The image is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame — no glass, no mount. It has a more textural, tactile feel than a flat print and suits a relaxed, warm interior brilliantly. Arrives ready to hang. Available in a range of canvas size options.

Paper finish: Luster vs Museum — Luster art paper has a soft sheen that makes colours feel vibrant and warm — ideal if your office has subdued or artificial lighting. Museum quality paper is a premium flat matte that gives a refined, understated look — brilliant in bright, naturally lit rooms where glare could be an issue.

Shabby chic art typically features earthy neutrals, dusty pinks, warm creams and aged tones that sit comfortably in bedrooms, living rooms, kitchens and home offices alike. What is artwork for an office?

Artwork for an office is any wall art — prints, framed pieces or canvas — chosen specifically to suit a working environment, whether that is a professional workspace or a home office. The best office art tends to use calming, neutral or nature-inspired imagery that helps reduce visual noise and makes a space feel pleasant to spend time in. Shabby chic botanical and floral art prints are a popular choice because their muted, soft palettes are easy to live with all day. A well-chosen set of prints can make an office feel more personal, more inspiring and far less like a blank, corporate room.

How to Hang Artwork for an Office — A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall you actually look at while you work — above the desk, opposite your chair or on the wall beside a window. Avoid walls in direct strong sunlight to protect your prints over time.

2. Decide on your layout: For a set of 3 prints, a straight horizontal row at eye level is the most classic and effective arrangement. Mark the centre of your wall space lightly in pencil, then space each print evenly outward from there — around 5 to 8 cm between each print looks clean and balanced.

3. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is noticeable on a set of three. Use a spirit level or a simple free phone app to make sure all three prints sit at exactly the same height before you fix them in place.

4. Step back and check: Before making any permanent holes, hold the prints up against the wall (use a friend or some masking tape) and step back to check the spacing and height feel right from where you normally sit at your desk — eye level seated is the golden rule for office art.

5. Fix securely: Use appropriate fixings for your wall type. Framed and canvas-wrapped options from AboutWallArt arrive ready to hang, so no extra fittings are needed — just fix and enjoy.

Unframed Print — The print is delivered flat and ready for you to frame yourself. A great choice if you already have a favourite frame style at home or want to match existing frames in your office. Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight away — no need to source a frame or worry about sizing. The most convenient option if you want a polished, finished look on your office wall without any extra effort. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper finish, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The art is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden frame, giving a tactile, painted quality with no glass and no frame required. Ready to hang immediately. Ideal if you love a more relaxed, studio-style look — especially lovely for botanical and floral art. Available in multiple sizes.

Paper Finish: Luster vs Museum Quality — Luster art paper has a gentle semi-gloss finish that makes colours and soft blush tones feel vibrant and fresh. Museum quality paper is a smooth matte finish with a fine-art feel — beautiful for vintage, shabby chic and botanical styles where a softer, more understated look suits the artwork perfectly.

aiItems.content:
What are botanical prints framed?

Botanical prints framed are wall art prints featuring nature-inspired subjects — such as pressed flowers, ferns, foliage and blooms — printed onto quality art paper and presented in a frame, ready to hang. They draw on a long tradition of scientific botanical illustration but in modern home decor they are used decoratively to bring an organic, calming quality to a room. A framed set, like a set of 3, creates an instant gallery-wall effect with coordinated compositions that share a colour palette and theme. They suit a wide range of interiors, from farmhouse and cottage styles to minimal and Scandi-influenced spaces, and work especially well in offices, living rooms and hallways where a touch of nature makes the room feel more grounded and considered.

How to Hang and Style Botanical Prints Framed as a Set of 3

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of your wall to see how the compositions sit together before you make a single hole. A horizontal row works best for most office walls and above desks — aim for an even gap of around 5–8 cm between each print so they read as a set.

2. Find your centre point: Measure the total width of all three prints plus the two gaps, then find the midpoint of your wall space. Mark this lightly with a pencil — it becomes the hanging point for your middle print, keeping the whole set perfectly balanced.

3. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit roughly at eye level (about 145–150 cm from the floor in most rooms). Above a desk, you can hang them slightly higher — around 15–20 cm above the top of your monitor or desk accessories — so they're visible without being too close.

4. Use a spirit level: Once your first print is up, use a small spirit level across the top edge before fixing the remaining two. Even a slight tilt is very visible across a three-print set, so this step saves a lot of time.

5. Step back and adjust: Once all three are hung, step back to the opposite side of the room and view them as a whole. Small adjustments now are much easier than after you've finished decorating around them.

Botanical Prints Framed: Which Option is Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print only, on your choice of Luster art paper or Museum quality paper. Great if you already have frames you love or want to source your own to match your existing decor exactly. Lightest and most affordable option; you handle the framing.

Framed Print — Your chosen art paper (Luster or Museum quality) presented in a frame, arriving ready to hang straight away. No need to source a frame separately or worry about sizing — the most convenient choice if you want to get the prints on the wall quickly. Available in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a sturdy frame, giving a gallery-style finish with no glass. No additional framing needed; arrives ready to hang. A great pick if you prefer a more relaxed, textural look rather than a traditional framed print. Available in a range of size options.

Luster Art Paper — A semi-gloss surface that keeps colours bright and crisp. Works especially well for the lighter purple and beige tones in this botanical set. A versatile, popular finish for both framed and unframed prints.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium fine-art surface with a slightly deeper colour response, bringing out the richness of the darker olive greens and near-black blooms in this set. Ideal if you want the most gallery-quality result.

Framed Print — Your print arrives mounted and framed, ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping required. A brilliant time-saver. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper inside the frame. Multiple size options to suit your wall.

content.metaDescription: Bring calm, nature-inspired style to your office with this navy & sage botanical art set of 3 — perfect for a serene, focused workspace. Free UK shipping!
content.productDescription:
Bring a breath of the natural world into your home office with this gorgeous set of botanical art prints, each one featuring a softly composed floral bouquet painted in muted navy blue, dusty periwinkle, warm taupe, and sage green against a clean white background. The three prints share the same cool, nature-inspired palette but each bouquet is its own thing — one leans into creamy blooms and broad leaves, the centre piece layers deep indigo flowers with trailing clusters, and the third features delicate fern fronds alongside airy sprigs. Together they feel collected and considered, like pages torn from a beautiful vintage botanical journal.

I love this set for a home office or workspace because the palette is genuinely calming — those soft navies and earthy greens are easy on the eye during a long work day, without feeling cold or clinical. The shabby chic watercolour style gives them just enough character to make your desk area feel personal and curated rather than plain. If you've been searching for something that's quietly beautiful without being fussy, this is it.

What's Included with Botanical Art Prints | Navy Blue & Sage Floral Bouquet Wall Art | Set of 3

  • A set of 3 individual botanical art prints, each featuring a unique navy blue and sage green floral bouquet illustration on a clean white background
  • Printed in the UK using fade-resistant pigment inks, designed for indoor display
  • Framed and canvas-wrapped options arrive ready to hang, saving you the time and hassle of hunting for a frame that fits — the unframed option is the print only
  • Choose between unframed and framed options in multiple sizes and in Luster or Museum quality; also available in wrapped canvas size options

How to Style Botanical Art in Your Office or Home Workspace

My favourite way to hang this set is in a straight horizontal row at eye level above a desk or console — equal gaps between each print, all centred on the same invisible line. Because the bouquets are portrait in composition and vary slightly in visual weight, that even, structured hang keeps things feeling intentional and neat rather than scattered. I'd keep the surrounding space fairly minimal so the prints can breathe. A simple wooden desk, a neutral linen chair, and a small plant on the desk and you've got a workspace that genuinely feels good to sit in.

The navy and sage palette sits beautifully against warm white, pale grey, or even a soft greige wall — so it works whether your office is bright and airy or a little cosier. If you're decorating a smaller space, the right-hand print with its delicate fern detail works alone as a single piece above a narrow shelf or beside a bookcase. For more styling ideas, have a browse through our full botanical art collection — there's plenty of inspiration in there.

Picking the Right Size and Finish for Your Space

Before you choose your size, hold a piece of paper or card against the wall where you're planning to hang the set and step back — it gives you a surprisingly honest sense of scale. For a standard desk or work wall, I'd suggest going at least to a medium size so the bouquet details really come through; too small and those lovely layered leaves and trailing flower clusters can get a bit lost. If you've got a wider wall or a generous run of space above a long desk, go bigger and let the set make more of a statement.

For finish, the Museum quality paper gives you the richest depth of colour — those deep navies really pop — while Luster is a lovely everyday choice that still looks brilliant. Both are printed with fade-resistant inks so they'll stay looking fresh for years. If you prefer something with more texture and dimension, the wrapped canvas option is worth a look. Scroll down to see how each size looks in an office before you decide — there's a size-guide image below showing every option in the room.

aiItems.content:
What is botanical art?

Botanical art is a style of illustration that depicts plants, flowers, leaves, and natural botanical subjects in careful, often beautiful detail — rooted in the tradition of scientific illustration but loved today as a decorative art form in its own right. It ranges from precise, vintage-style engravings to loose, painterly watercolour compositions like the navy and sage floral prints in this set. Botanical art prints are one of the most popular choices for home offices and living spaces because they bring a sense of calm, nature-inspired beauty to any wall without feeling loud or trend-dependent. They suit a wide range of interior styles — from shabby chic and vintage to modern and minimal — and they work equally well as a single statement piece or grouped as a set of prints.

How to Hang a Set of Botanical Art Prints in Your Office

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of the wall you have in mind. Decide on the order — for this set, placing the largest-feeling bouquet in the centre works beautifully — and measure the total width including the gaps you want between each print.

2. Find your centre point: Mark the centre of your wall space lightly with a pencil, then measure outward equally in each direction so all three prints sit symmetrically. Eye level is roughly 145–150 cm from the floor to the centre of each print.

3. Use a spirit level: Even a small wonk will catch your eye every time you sit at your desk, so take a minute to check each print is level before you commit. A small spirit level or a free phone app both do the job.

4. Keep gaps consistent: For a clean, intentional look, aim for an equal gap between each print — 5 to 8 cm works well for most sizes. Too wide and the set starts to feel like three separate pieces rather than one cohesive grouping.

5. Stand back and check: Before you're fully done, step back to the opposite side of the room and look at the set as a whole. Adjust if needed — it only takes a moment and makes all the difference.

Choosing the Right Print Option for Your Botanical Art

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want a specific frame style. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no separate frame shopping needed. A brilliant choice if you want a polished, finished result with minimal effort. Available in Luster art paper or Museum quality paper, in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image wrapping around the edges. No frame needed at all — just hang and enjoy. Gives the set a contemporary, gallery-style feel and works especially well in modern or minimal office spaces.

Luster Paper — A semi-sheen finish that gives vibrant, true-to-life colour with a slight sheen. Handles the navy blues and soft greens in this set beautifully and is a great all-round choice for wall art prints.

Museum Quality Paper — A premium matte fine-art paper that gives the deepest, richest colour depth — the dark indigo tones in this botanical set look especially striking on this finish. Ideal if you want the highest quality result.
